🌎 BEYOND THE 956

A Dallas County jury found Dallas rapper Yella Beezy guilty of capital murder Wednesday, November 11, 2026, in the 2020 murder-for-hire killing of fellow rapper MO3 — exactly six years to the day after MO3 was shot and killed on Interstate 35 in Dallas.

Yella Beezy, 35, whose legal name is Markies Conway, was convicted of capital murder by remuneration, or murder for hire. Because prosecutors did not seek the death penalty, the conviction carries an automatic sentence of life in prison without the possibility of parole.

Prosecutors alleged Conway paid Kewon White $40,000 to carry out the killing. White, identified by prosecutors as the gunman, was convicted of capital murder in September 2026 and sentenced to life in prison without parole. Conway pleaded not guilty and denied any involvement in the killing, and he can appeal the verdict.

MO3, 28, whose real name was Melvin Noble, was driving on Interstate 35 in south Dallas around noon on November 11, 2020, when White pulled alongside him and opened fire, authorities said. Prosecutors said the killing grew out of a years-long feud between the two rappers.

A third defendant, Devin Brown, is also charged with capital murder in connection with MO3's death and is still awaiting trial.

Update — November 19, 2026

Devin Maurice Brown, the third defendant in the case, pleaded guilty on Thursday morning in a Dallas County courtroom and was sentenced to 10 years in prison, NBC 5 Dallas-Fort Worth reported. Brown pleaded guilty to a lesser murder charge, and his drug charges were dropped, according to FOX 4. Judge Chika Anyiam accepted the plea deal; under its terms, Brown waived his right to appeal and will have to serve at least half of his sentence, the judge said. Prosecutors had accused Brown of helping pinpoint MO3's location before the November 2020 shooting. He had faced a capital murder charge that carried an automatic sentence of life in prison without parole, and he has been jailed since his arrest in 2020. With Brown's plea, all three men charged in MO3's killing have now been sentenced: Conway and White to life without parole, and Brown to 10 years.

Update — November 26, 2026

Markies Conway, the Dallas rapper known as Yella Beezy, filed a notice of appeal on Friday, November 20, challenging his November 11 capital murder conviction and life-without-parole sentence in the 2020 killing of Dallas rapper MO3, according to court documents reported by FOX 4. The notice was filed at 3:25 p.m. in Dallas County Criminal District Court No. 7, case F25-00154, through attorney Michael Mowla, and it does not spell out the specific legal grounds the defense plans to argue. Conway is serving his sentence at the W.F. Ramsey Unit in Rosharon, Texas. A notice of appeal does not overturn a conviction; the sentence remains in effect while the Texas Court of Appeals reviews the case.

Correction: Our November 19 update said that with Devin Brown’s guilty plea, all three men charged in MO3’s killing had been sentenced. That was incorrect. There were four defendants. Jerry Johnson, whom prosecutors accuse of acting as the middleman who arranged payments between Conway and Kewon White, is still charged with capital murder and awaiting trial, and it is not yet clear whether his case will go to a jury or end in a plea, FOX 4 reported. Johnson is presumed innocent.

Sources: WorldStar (@worldstar) on Instagram; CNN; XXL; AllHipHop. NBC 5 Dallas-Fort Worth — "MO3 murder case ends with third defendant sentenced to 10 years," Nov. 19, 2026; FOX 4 News — "Yella Beezy co-defendant Devin Brown expected to plead guilty," Nov. 19, 2026; FOX 4 News, Nov. 24, 2026, via KIIZ/iHeart, Nov. 25, 2026; Baller Alert; TX Gazette, Nov. 24, 2026.

title: Beyond the 956: Yella Beezy found guilty of capital murder in MO3 killing, sentenced to life without parole
